stem.en: Look at those black clouds! It ___ rain.

why.en: We can see the clouds now, so we use be going to for this prediction: it is going to rain.
why.uz: Bulutlar hozir koʻrinib turibdi, shuning uchun bashorat uchun be going to: it is going to rain.
why.ru: Тучи видны сейчас, поэтому для прогноза используем be going to: it is going to rain.

stem.en: The phone is ringing. — OK, I ___ answer it.

why.en: A decision made at the moment of speaking uses will + the base verb: I will answer it.
why.uz: Gapirish paytida qabul qilingan qaror will + feʼlning asosiy shakli bilan ifodalanadi: I will answer it.
why.ru: Решение, принятое в момент речи, выражается will + начальная форма: I will answer it.

stem.en: We ___ visit Samarkand in May. We've already booked the hotel.

why.en: A plan made before now (the hotel is booked) uses be going to + verb: we are going to visit.
why.uz: Oldindan tuzilgan reja (mehmonxona band qilingan) be going to + feʼl bilan: we are going to visit.
why.ru: План, принятый заранее (отель забронирован): be going to + глагол: we are going to visit.

stem.en: I think our team ___ win the game tomorrow.

why.en: For an opinion about the future after I think, use will + the base verb.
why.uz: I think dan keyin kelajak haqidagi fikr will + feʼlning asosiy shakli bilan aytiladi.
why.ru: Мнение о будущем после I think выражается will + начальная форма глагола.

why.en: The present perfect is have/has + past participle; with I we use have: I have never eaten.
why.uz: Present Perfect: have/has + uchinchi shakl; I bilan have: I have never eaten.
why.ru: Present Perfect: have/has + третья форма; с I — have: I have never eaten.

stem.en: Bekzod has ___ seen this film. He doesn't want to see it again.

why.en: Already in a positive sentence means the action happened before now.
why.uz: Already tasdiq gapda harakat hozirgacha sodir boʻlib boʻlganini bildiradi.
why.ru: Already в утвердительном предложении значит, что действие уже произошло.

stem.en: ___ your parents ever travelled by plane?

why.en: Travelled with ever is the present perfect, and parents is plural: Have your parents...?
why.uz: Ever bilan travelled — Present Perfect; parents koʻplikda: Have your parents...?
why.ru: Travelled с ever — Present Perfect; parents — множественное число: Have your parents...?

options.en: She has lost her keys again.
She has lose her keys again.
She have lost her keys again.
She has losted her keys again.

why.en: Present perfect with she: has + past participle (lost).
why.uz: She bilan Present Perfect: has + uchinchi shakl (lost).
why.ru: Present Perfect с she: has + третья форма (lost).

stem.en: We don't have ___ time. The bus leaves in five minutes.

why.en: Time here is uncountable, and in negatives we use much with uncountable nouns.
why.uz: Bu yerda time sanalmaydigan ot; inkor gapda sanalmaydigan otlar bilan much ishlatiladi.
why.ru: Time здесь неисчисляемое; в отрицании с неисчисляемыми используется much.

stem.en: There aren't ___ students in the classroom yet.

why.en: Students can be counted, so we use many; no is wrong after aren't (double negative).
why.uz: Students sanaladi, shuning uchun many; aren't dan keyin no notoʻgʻri (ikki inkor).
why.ru: Students исчисляемое, поэтому many; no после aren't неверно (двойное отрицание).

stem.en: I'd like ___ water, please. I'm very thirsty.

why.en: Water is uncountable, and in requests and offers we use some.
why.uz: Water sanalmaydi; iltimos va taklif gaplarida some ishlatiladi.
why.ru: Water неисчисляемое; в просьбах и предложениях используется some.

stem.en: There's ___ juice left in the fridge. Can you buy some?

why.en: There's no + noun means zero; any needs a negative verb, and none is not used before a noun.
why.uz: There's no + ot «umuman yoʻq» degani; any inkor feʼl bilan keladi, none ot oldidan ishlatilmaydi.
why.ru: There's no + существительное — «совсем нет»; any требует отрицательного глагола, none не ставится перед существительным.

stem.en: You look tired. You ___ go to bed early tonight.

why.en: For advice we use should + the base verb, with no to.
why.uz: Maslahat uchun should + feʼlning asosiy shakli, to siz.
why.ru: Для совета используется should + начальная форма, без to.

stem.en: In our school, students ___ wear a uniform. It's a rule.

why.en: A rule is an obligation: students (they) have to wear a uniform.
why.uz: Qoida — majburiyat: students (they) have to wear a uniform.
why.ru: Правило — это обязанность: students (they) have to wear a uniform.

stem.en: You ___ eat so many sweets. They're bad for your teeth.

why.en: This is advice not to do something, so we use shouldn't; don't have to means it is not necessary.
why.uz: Bu biror narsani qilmaslik haqida maslahat, shuning uchun shouldn't; don't have to «shart emas» degani.
why.ru: Это совет чего-то не делать, поэтому shouldn't; don't have to значит «не обязательно».

stem.en: Does your brother ___ work on Saturdays?

why.en: After does, use the base form: Does he have to...? (not has to).
why.uz: Does dan keyin asosiy shakl keladi: Does he have to...? (has to emas).
why.ru: После does нужна начальная форма: Does he have to...? (не has to).
